hook: Google Cloud grew *103%*. Alphabet's shares still fell 8%
tldr: Alphabet's cloud revenue doubled, but heavy AI spending pushed free cash flow negative and shares fell after hours.

beats.what: Q3 revenue $127.6B (+25%). Cloud $30.7B (+103%). Capex $51.4B. Free cash flow −$9.1B.
beats.why: Alphabet is spending heavily on AI data centres and chips.
beats.care: Investors are questioning the cost of the AI build-out, per The Hindu and XTB.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Alphabet, Google's parent, reported Q3 revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25%. Google Cloud more than doubled to $30.7 billion. But capex (spending on data centres and chips) rose 114% to $51.4 billion, above operating cash flow, so free cash flow was minus $9.1 billion. Earnings per share were $2.12 against expectations near $3, partly due to an $8.7 billion investment loss. Shares fell 8.25% after hours, per XTB. The Hindu adds that AI-powered search raises questions about Google's ad business.

cards.title: 🧠 Free cash flow?
cards.body: Cash left after paying for operations and big investments. Negative means the company spent more than it brought in. Alphabet also raised about $28.7 billion through bonds, per XTB.
